description: Table 2 is a single-panel rendered data table, presented as five columns with a blue-grey header band and alternating white/pale-grey body rows. The column headers are "Composition (wt.%)", "Density (g·cm⁻³)", "TE (%)", "UTS (MPa)" and "Thermal-mechanical processes". Eight alloy rows are tabulated, each composition followed by a bracketed reference number printed in blue: Fe–15Mn–10Al-0.86C–5Ni [19], Fe–23Mn-1.5Al-0.3C [48], Fe–27Mn-12Al-0.9C [24], Fe–11Mn-10Al-1.2C [51], Fe–30Mn-11Al-1.2C [34], Fe–21Mn-10Al–1C–5Ni [54], Fe–29Mn-9.4Al-0.3C [47] and Fe–28Mn–9Al–0.9C–5Ni [53]. Tabulated densities lie between 6.29 and 7.4 g·cm⁻³, TE between 17.8 and 98.9 %, and UTS between 757 and 1620 MPa. Process routes named are Cold rolling-annealing, Hot rolling-solution, Cold rolling-water quenching, Cold rolling-annealing-aging, Solution-aging, Solution-water quenching and Cold rolling-annealing-aging. The extreme mechanical pairings are Fe–23Mn-1.5Al-0.3C [48] (98.9 % TE at 840 MPa) and Fe–28Mn–9Al–0.9C–5Ni [53] (20.3 % TE at 1620 MPa); the lowest density is 6.29 g·cm⁻³ for Fe–30Mn–11Al-1.2C [34]. The table demonstrates that strength–ductility combinations of Fe-Mn-C-Al low-density steels scatter widely and track the thermal-mechanical route applied, with cold rolling plus annealing/aging routes generally giving the higher UTS values.

observations.observation: The table has five columns headed Composition (wt.%), Density (g·cm⁻³), TE (%), UTS (MPa) and Thermal-mechanical processes, and contains eight data rows.

The composition column lists Fe–15Mn–10Al-0.86C–5Ni [19], Fe–23Mn-1.5Al-0.3C [48], Fe–27Mn-12Al-0.9C [24], Fe–11Mn-10Al-1.2C [51], Fe–30Mn-11Al-1.2C [34], Fe–21Mn-10Al–1C–5Ni [54], Fe–29Mn-9.4Al-0.3C [47] and Fe–28Mn–9Al–0.9C–5Ni [53], each followed by a bracketed reference number printed in blue.
Density values range from 6.29 g·cm⁻³ (Fe–30Mn–11Al-1.2C [34]) to 7.4 g·cm⁻³ (Fe–29Mn-9.4Al-0.3C [47]).
Fe–23Mn-1.5Al-0.3C [48] has the largest total elongation in the table, TE = 98.9 %, together with the second-lowest UTS, 840 MPa.
Fe–28Mn–9Al–0.9C–5Ni [53] has the largest ultimate tensile strength in the table, UTS = 1620 MPa, at TE = 20.3 %.
Fe–15Mn–10Al-0.86C–5Ni [19] is listed with density 6.71 g·cm⁻³, TE 18.0 % and UTS 1548 MPa after Cold rolling-annealing.

Thermal-mechanical process entries are Cold rolling-annealing, Hot rolling-solution, Cold rolling-water quenching, Cold rolling-annealing-aging, Solution-aging, Solution-water quenching and Cold rolling-annealing-aging.
The caption states that TE and UTS represent total elongation and ultimate tensile strength, respectively.
The caption states the table compares mechanical properties of low-density steels under different thermal-mechanical processes.
The citing text states that Table 2 summarizes the mechanical properties of various forged plates obtained under different thermal-mechanical processes.

The citing text asserts that the tensile strength and total elongation of low-density steels strongly depend on cold rolling-annealing and aging hardening, because the type, distribution and size of precipitates are susceptible to annealing/aging temperatures and times.
